raw.description: Hardcoded secret in the environment variable JWT_SECRET is used for signing JWT tokens. If this secret is not properly secured, it can lead to token forgery.
raw.exploit: An attacker with access to the environment variables can forge JWT tokens.

raw.description: CSRF protection is implemented using csurf middleware, but the CSRF token is not properly handled in the frontend. The token is hardcoded in the frontend code.
raw.exploit: An attacker can perform CSRF attacks if they can predict or obtain the CSRF token.

raw.description: Improper access control in the /api/projects endpoint allows any authenticated user to view all projects if they are an admin, but there is no verification of the user's role in the frontend.
raw.exploit: An attacker can modify the frontend code to change their role and access unauthorized data.

raw.description: The role state in the frontend is hardcoded to 'member', which could lead to incorrect assumptions about user permissions.
raw.exploit: An attacker can modify the frontend code to change their role and potentially access unauthorized functionality.
